issues.where: NibKit/Sources/FeatTextDoc/BlockComments.swift:1844-1851 (CommentsPanelModel.open), :1865-1874 (reveal), :1777-1785 (rebuild handling `requested`, which also runs from init and after postDraft at :1838), :1605-1609 (row context menu 'Reply')
issues.problem: Opening a thread in the Comments tab calls reveal(row). reveal runs editor.focus(id, at:), which makes the document's BlockTextView first responder, and then sets the text view's selection to the commented words. This happens on every row tap, on the context-menu 'Reply', on panel.open {block} (the block menu's 'Show Comments'), and on the new thread opened right after posting from the tab's composer. On iPad with a hardware keyboard, a user who opens a thread (or presses Reply, or keeps typing after posting) and types a reply is typing into the document, and the first key replaces the commented words. On a software keyboard the document's keyboard appears over the docked tab or the sheet (compact width). The reply field is never focused. When panel.open carries {block}, reveal also runs during the @StateObject initialiser (CommentsPanelModel.init → rebuild → open), so becomeFirstResponder, scrollToItem and layoutIfNeeded run inside a SwiftUI graph update.
issues.fix: Split 'show' from 'focus'. In open(row), only scroll: `editor.reveal(block: id, animated: !UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled)`. Keep editor.focus plus the selection for the explicit 'Show in Document' action (showInDocument) only. For 'Reply' (context menu), add `@Published var focusReply = false` to CommentThreadModel. Set it after expanding, and in CommentThreadView bind `.onChange(of: model.focusReply) { if $1 { replyFocused = true; model.focusReply = false } }`. Move the reveal that rebuild triggers for `requested` out of init: record the target, and perform it from the panel's `.onAppear` or a `Task { @MainActor in ... }`. Add a test: build CommentsPanelModel with an open editor and params {block}, call open(row), and assert the paragraph's text view is not first responder and the block text is unchanged.

issues.problem: D-115 auto-linking can save links that point to half-typed addresses. The typing trigger arms on any punctuation (':' '/' '.' '@' are all in .punctuationCharacters), and every later key pushes the pass back. The pass then runs after a 1.2 s pause even when the caret is still inside or at the end of an address being typed. Here is how a link goes wrong. The user types 'see https://exa' and pauses. block.update links 'https://exa'. F047's configureText resets typingAttributes, so the rest ('mple.com/notes') is typed unlinked. Every later pass skips the full match, because `touches(out, m.range) { $0.link != nil }` is true. The result is a permanent link to https://exa (or 'mailto:ada@exam', 'http://www.goo'). It stays until the user finds it and removes it by hand.
issues.fix: In link(_:in:), when the pass was started by typing (not by focus leaving), read the focused text view's caret for that block. Skip matches with `NSLocationInRange(caret, m.range) || NSMaxRange(m.range) == caret`, so an address is linked only once a space, newline or caret move ends it, and on focus leave. Also let a new match replace an earlier auto-link that is a strict prefix of it. In linked(_:skipping:), when every link run inside m.range has `link.url` equal to the URL of its own text (a link auto-linking made), re-apply the new link over the whole m.range instead of skipping it. Add a test: link 'see https://exa', append 'mple.com ' to the text, run AutoLinker.linked again, and expect one link 'https://example.com' covering the whole address. Add a second test that a pass with the caret at the end of 'https://exa' links nothing.

issues.problem: Re-anchoring issues one block.editComment invocation per moved comment, so every keystroke before a comment adds 1 + N commits (N = comments whose range moved). Each commit rewrites the whole block record, adds an undo record and a sync op, and triggers the editor's reloadFromModel/BlockSnapshotPlan/diffable apply over every block, plus the Comments tab and Outline rebuilds. Typing near the start of a paragraph with several comments in a long document multiplies the per-keystroke cost, and the highlight visibly jumps back a character between the text commit and the keeper's commit.
issues.fix: In flush(), collect every move and range edit for a group into one `CommandIDs.batch` invocation: `Invocation(command: CommandIDs.batch, params: ["calls": calls], principal: .user, group: job.group)`. That gives one commit and one undo merge per keystroke. Keep the per-call guards (still at the stored range, has text) while building `calls`. Add a test that types three characters before two comments and asserts the number of commits observed per keystroke is 2 (text + one batch).

issues.problem: The prefix/suffix diff slides an insertion or deletion to the rightmost position inside a run of repeated characters. When the typed character equals the first character of a commented word, the comment grows over it. For example, with a comment on 'blocks' at [6,6] in 'Hello blocks', typing 'b' at offset 6 gives Edit(7,7,8) and the range becomes [6,7] 'bblocks' instead of [7,6]. The same happens with a deletion next to a range end.
issues.fix: When computing the edit, also compute the leftmost equivalent start (`pMin`: walk p back while a[p-1] == b[p-1+delta] for insertions, the mirror for deletions). In map(_:through:), when a range boundary lies in [pMin, p], treat the insertion as outside the range: for start, use pMin when range.location >= pMin; for end, keep x when x <= p. Add the 'bblocks' case to testRangesMoveThroughEdits.

issues.problem: Printing is reachable only through the ⌘P TextDocHooks key. TextDocViewController never becomes first responder itself, so the key is live only while a block text view has the caret. There is no touch path (iPhone, or iPad without a keyboard), no entry in the command bar, and nothing plugins or the AI can call. print.present is F067's and is still a placeholder on main.
issues.fix: Keep the hook for now. Document in FeatTextDocExtrasFeature that F067's print.present for .textDocument must use TextDocPageRenderer (for example `TextDocPrinter.present(doc:session:)` made callable without an editor, taking the blocks from app.workspace). File docs/contract-requests/F103-print.md so F067 routes print.present {doc} for text documents to it and registers ⌘P as a KeyCommandDescriptor with `docKinds` and `sessionParams` naming the document. In the meantime, let the editor serve ⌘P while no block is focused: override `canBecomeFirstResponder` in a TextDocHooks editorObserver-installed responder, or make the hook set non-empty through the shell's key path once print.present exists.

issues.problem: A comment the user has typed can be lost. The popover and sheet composer call dismiss() before block.comment runs. If the command is refused (the words' range no longer fits because the block changed through sync, the assistant or another window, the document got locked, and so on), only a toast remains and the typed comment is gone. In the Comments tab, resolveDraft sets draft = nil when the commented words are deleted meanwhile, which removes the composer together with its @State text.
issues.fix: In newComment, run the command first and dismiss only on success. Keep the composer open with isPosting while it runs (pass isPosting like the tab does), and on failure leave the text in place. Also map the range through the block's text changes before posting (the same CommentAnchors.edit/map that resolveDraft uses, from the text captured at present time). In resolveDraft, do not drop a draft whose words were deleted. Keep it with an empty excerpt ('The commented text was deleted.') and disable Comment, or fall back to a whole-block range, so the typed text survives.

issues.problem: ⇧⌘M while no text is edited composes on `lastSelection`, a selection that is no longer visible and may be arbitrarily old. It is never cleared after a comment is posted, so the next ⇧⌘M opens a second composer on the same words. When the Comments tab is already on screen, a repeated ⇧⌘M with identical params does nothing, because `.onChange(of: params)` does not fire for an equal value. The user then has no composer after pressing Cancel and trying again.
issues.fix: Clear TextDocExtrasState.lastSelection when block.comment succeeds for it (in newComment and postDraft) and when the editor scrolls the block off screen or another block gets focus. Add a nonce to keyParams, `"request": .string(NibID.make().raw)`, so every key press reaches the tab. Add a test that calls apply() twice with the same {block, range, compose} after cancelDraft() and expects a draft again.

issues.problem: These are memory, main-thread and trust gaps. Every image block is decoded up front at up to 3× the column width and kept in the layout for the whole export (about 8 MB each at A4, so an image-heavy document of 100 images holds close to 1 GB). The whole PDF is built in memory by pdfData on the main actor, which draws every page there and blocks the UI on long documents. Printing lays out (and decodes) everything on the first numberOfPages call. Link annotations are written for any `.link` value, including nib:// internal ids and schemes such as file: or javascript: that came from AI, plugin or synced content.
issues.fix: Store only the image's pixel size in Unit (CGImageSourceCopyPropertiesAtIndex), and decode it in draw(page:) inside `autoreleasepool` with BlockImageLoader, releasing it after the page. Render the PDF off the main actor with `UIGraphicsPDFRenderer.writePDF(to:)` straight to the job URL (TextDocPrintSnapshot is already value-captured). Wrap each page in autoreleasepool. In PrintTextFlow.draw, annotate only URLs whose scheme is in AutoLinker.schemes.

issues.where: NibKit/Sources/FeatTextDoc/TextDocOutlinePanel.swift:302-324 (row), BlockComments.swift:1488-1500 and :1560-1562 (draft and expanded-row backgrounds); tests
issues.problem: Design gate gaps. DESIGN §15.7 requires every new screen to add its snapshots (Light, Dark, Reduce Transparency, Increase Contrast, AX3), but only the thread card and the composer are snapshotted, not TextDocOutlinePanel or TextDocCommentsPanel. Outline rows activate through .onTapGesture, so Full Keyboard Access cannot focus them or show a focus ring. The draft composer and the expanded row put NibField (fill4) and secondary NibButtons (fill3) on a fill3 rounded rectangle, which the Slop checklist bans as nested backgrounds.
issues.fix: Add NibSnapshot.images tests for TextDocOutlinePanel (with the fixture's heading plus nested H2/H3) and TextDocCommentsPanel (list, expanded thread, draft) over all NibSnapshot.Variant cases. Wrap each outline row in `Button { open(e) } label: { NibOutlineRow(...) }.buttonStyle(.plain)`; the chevron keeps its own inner button. Drop the fill3 background from the draft composer and the expanded row, and mark the expanded row with NibOutlineRow-style selection or a hairline separator so the fields sit directly on the panel.

issues.problem: Hand-rolled styling instead of tokens. The TextKit 1 comment rule builds its own dash pattern from `NibStroke.hairline * 2`, although NibDesign v2 has `NibStroke.layerDash` for CAShapeLayer. Print margins (54 pt), the type scale (0.7) and the footer band are literals with no contract request (DESIGN §15.6). Printed headings are rebuilt from documentBody's descriptor plus a bold trait instead of `NibUIFont.documentHeading(level)`.
issues.fix: Use `rules.lineDashPattern = NibStroke.layerDash`, or file docs/contract-requests/F103-dot-dash.md for a dotted layer pattern matching `.patternDot` and cite it. File docs/contract-requests/F103-print-metrics.md (print margin, print type scale) and reference it on TextDocPrintMetrics. Build heading fonts as `UIFont(descriptor: NibUIFont.documentHeading(level).fontDescriptor, size: printSize)`.

issues.problem: Several risky paths have no test. Auto-linking a partially typed address (the major above) is untested. So is the Comments tab's side effects on editor focus and selection. The keeper is not tested under rapid typing (the `pending` continuation when commits arrive before flush), nor with a boundary character that repeats. Nothing tests the TextKit 1 highlight path or the print path (TextDocPageRenderer with paper nil and a UIPrintPaperRect-like size).
issues.fix: Add these tests. (1) Two block.update commits before `keeper.idle()`, asserting the final ranges equal a single rebase. (2) The 'bblocks' anchor case. (3) The partial-URL and caret-at-end auto-link cases. (4) open(row) leaves the text view unfocused. (5) Force TextKit 1 (touch `cell.textView.layoutManager`), then decorate and assert a sublayer named 'textdocextras.comment.marks' with a non-empty path. (6) TextDocPageRenderer(snapshot:paper:nil) with a stubbed paperRect/printableRect subclass returns numberOfPages ≥ 1 and draws without crashing.
